Can gold hold $4,000 with an October rate hike still in play?
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) - Hotter-than-expected consumer prices have put an October rate hike back in play , pushing real bond yields higher and dragging gold prices below a critical near-term support level. However, commodity analysts expect support to continue to hold at $4,000 an ounce, as the Federal Reserve is unlikely to raise interest rates just one week before American voters head to the polls for the 2026 midterm elections. In a note Wednesday, Ryan McKay, Director of Commodity Strategy at TD Securities, noted that gold’s inability to break through resistance at $4,200 has prompted speculative fund managers to liquidate their long positions, while the disappointing inflation numbers have added fuel to the fire.

U.S. Treasury's gold revaluation could restart the ‘debasement trade' as yield pressures fade – UBP's Kinsella
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) – Gold has likely seen the worst of its Treasury-yield-driven losses, and once the Iran situation improves and Fed rate hike expectations ease, the Treasury department itself could provide a new tailwind for bullion prices between now and year-end, according to Peter Kinsella, Head of Investment Services for the UK at Swiss private bank UBP. Kinsella noted that gold has traded lower since the Federal Reserve’s 25-basis-point rate hike in September. “The downward move has been rather muted, considering the huge rise in both nominal and real inflation-adjusted interest rates,” he said. “US 10-year yields have risen to highs of 5.30%, and 10-year TIPS yields (a proxy for real interest rate expectations) have risen to levels of just below 3%.”
